stories.headline: Iran supreme leader’s adviser says Trump must release $24bn to save peace talks
stories.summary: A senior adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, has stated that nuclear negotiations with the US are at a deadlock. The adviser, Mohsen Rezaei, says President Donald Trump must agree to release $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets to revive talks. This demand is seen as a test of trust for the US, with Iran wanting to gauge America's commitment to reaching an agreement. The release of the frozen assets has become a major stumbling block in potential peace talks between the two countries. If the US fails to comply, Iran has warned that the situation could escalate, with the US potentially "entering into a dark period". The stalemate continues, with the fate of a potential peace deal hanging in the balance. The $24 billion in question is a key point of contention in the negotiations.

stories.headline: North Korean leader Kim showcases new warship ahead of visit by China's Xi
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has showcased a new warship, the 5,000-tonne destroyer Kang Kon, ahead of a visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping. Kim visited the warship on Thursday as it underwent capability tests, according to the Korean Central News Agency. He was accompanied by his teenage daughter, who has been increasingly prominent in recent appearances. The visit comes as Xi is expected to meet Kim in Pyongyang next week, in a rare visit to the North Korean capital. The meeting is scheduled to take place, with Xi's trip aiming to strengthen ties between the two nations. Kim's inspection of the warship highlights North Korea's ongoing military development, as the country continues to enhance its defense capabilities. The visit by Xi is anticipated to further solidify the alliance between China and North Korea.

stories.headline: Germany fails to gain seat in UN Security Council election
stories.summary: Germany failed to secure a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, losing to Portugal and Austria. The country's bid was unsuccessful for the first time. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul suggested that Germany's support for Israel may have contributed to the loss of crucial votes. The UN Security Council consists of 15 members, with five permanent members - the United States, Russia, China, France, and the United Kingdom - and 10 elected members serving staggered two-year terms. The election allocates seats to different world regions. Germany's failure to gain a seat reflects a shift in global opinion, with some attributing it to opposition to the country's foreign policy and militarism. The outcome marks a significant setback for Germany's diplomatic efforts, highlighting the complexities of international relations and voting dynamics within the UN.

stories.headline: 'Mass invasion of migrants': JD Vance on teen stabbed by Indian-origin man in UK; draws Britain's response
stories.summary: US Senator JD Vance linked the murder of 18-year-old British student Henry Nowak to the UK's migration policies, sparking a diplomatic row. Nowak was fatally stabbed in Southampton by Vickrum Digwa, a man of Indian origin, in December. Vance blamed Britain's migrant policies for "civilizational decline" following the incident. The UK government swiftly rebuked Vance's comments, criticizing his attempt to connect the murder to migration. The incident occurred after Nowak was falsely accused of a racist attack. Vance's remarks drew a strong response from the UK, with officials dismissing his claims as unfounded and insensitive. The case has sparked a wider debate on migration and crime in the UK, with Vance's comments being widely condemned as inflammatory and inaccurate. The UK government has emphasized that the incident should not be used to stoke anti-migrant sentiment.

stories.headline: 'Final Fantasy VII Revelation' Will Conclude 7-Year Remake Journey In Spring 2027
stories.summary: Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the final installment in the remake trilogy, set to release in Spring 2027. The game will be available on multiple platforms, including PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam, Epic Games Store, and Xbox PC. Director Naoki Hamaguchi expressed excitement for the conclusion of the 7-year remake journey. The game is currently in development, with a simultaneous launch planned across all platforms. Final Fantasy VII Revelation will conclude the story, following the previous two installments. The announcement marks the final chapter in the remake trilogy, which has been in development since 2020, and fans can expect the game to be released in Spring 2027. The conclusion of the trilogy is highly anticipated, and the simultaneous launch will allow players to experience it together.

stories.headline: Yakuza Studio’s Next Game Is Performing Digital Necromancy On Tupac
stories.summary: Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio announced during Summer Game Fest that legendary rapper Tupac Shakur will appear in their upcoming game, Stranger Than Heaven. Tupac, who died in 1996, will be featured through digital necromancy. The studio had previously revealed another deceased person's likeness, Bunta Sugawara, in a cast trailer, for which they obtained permission. Stranger Than Heaven was previously known as Project Century, and its final name was revealed on June 7, 2025. The inclusion of Tupac's likeness in the game has sparked negative reactions, with many expressing disappointment and disapproval. The game is being developed by Yakuza Studio, known for their work on the Yakuza series, and is expected to feature a unique blend of music and gameplay. Further details about the game's storyline and features have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: vivo X300 Pro Photographer Kit sells out in pre-orders
stories.summary: The vivo X300 Pro Photographer Kit has sold out during its pre-order period, indicating strong demand for the flagship imaging smartphone. The kit, which enhances the photography experience with impressive zoom performance and a telephoto lens, was quickly snapped up by customers. The sell-out comes as vivo promotes its X80 5G model, featuring a 32MP front camera, ZEISS professional imaging, and a 50MP Ultra-sensing sensor. However, some customers have expressed disappointment at the kit's limited availability, with some online marketplaces and physical stores already showing out of stock. The vivo store's shipping restrictions have also affected some customers, such as those in Denmark, who are unable to purchase the kit due to shipping limitations. Despite this, the sell-out suggests a positive response to vivo's latest flagship offerings.

stories.headline: Unifi TV To Broadcast All 104 FIFA World Cup 2026 Matches For Less Than RM1 Per Match
stories.summary: Unifi TV has secured the rights to broadcast all 104 matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup live in Malaysia. The matches will be shown across three dedicated channels, offering comprehensive tournament coverage. Football fans can access the live matches for less than RM1 per match. This follows a strategic collaboration with major broadcasters to bring the tournament to local fans. In addition to Unifi TV, Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) will also be broadcasting the matches. The 2026 FIFA World Cup will feature 104 matches, and with this deal, Malaysian fans will have extensive coverage of the tournament. Unifi TV's viewing packages will provide live access to all matches, making it an affordable option for fans to watch the World Cup.

stories.headline: Updated NBA Finals Ticket Prices for Games 3, 4 at MSG After Knicks Take 2-0 Series Lead vs. Spurs
stories.summary: The New York Knicks' 2-0 series lead over the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals has driven up ticket prices for Games 3 and 4 at Madison Square Garden. According to Gametime, the get-in price for Game 3 surged to $11,736 after the Knicks' Game 2 win, up from $7,142 on Thursday afternoon. On StubHub, the cheapest ticket available for Game 3 costs $7,517. Demand for tickets has increased to five times its usual pace, with tickets for Game 4 selling at 10 times the usual speed. Courtside seats for Game 3 start at $50,000, with the most expensive ticket priced at $109,263. The median ticket price for Game 3 is $17,398, indicating high demand and limited availability.

stories.headline: NBA Finals: Brunson scores, Wembanyama misses, Knicks hold on to take 2-game lead over Spurs
stories.summary: The New York Knicks took a 2-0 lead in the NBA Finals, defeating the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 in Game 2. Jalen Brunson made the go-ahead free throw, securing the win after the Spurs' furious fourth-quarter comeback. The Knicks had led by 14 points with six minutes remaining but saw their lead dwindle. Victor Wembanyama missed a last-second shot, allowing the Knicks to hold on for the victory. The game was an intense back-and-forth contest, with the Knicks ultimately emerging with a one-point win. The Spurs' rally fell just short, and the Knicks now have a commanding lead in the series. The win marks a significant advantage for the Knicks as the series progresses.

stories.headline: Dana White Claps Back at Joe Rogan's UFC Freedom 250 Take
stories.summary: UFC president Dana White responded to commentator Joe Rogan's suggestion that the upcoming UFC Freedom 250 card is a "gimmick." The event is scheduled to take place on June 14 on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, D.C. White pushed back against Rogan's labeling, citing the participation of notable fighters like Alex Pereira. The exchange comes as the UFC prepares for the unique outdoor event, which has raised concerns about factors like insect attraction due to the large lighting rig around the octagon. Despite these challenges, White is promoting the event, set to occur next Sunday. The back-and-forth between White and Rogan highlights the buzz surrounding UFC Freedom 250, with the UFC CEO respecting Rogan's opinions while defending the event's legitimacy.

stories.headline: No more goodbyes: Has Indian cricket finally learned to move on?
stories.summary: Indian cricket has witnessed the retirement of several key players in 2025, including Rohit Sharma from Test cricket and Ravichandran Ashwin. Recently, Suryakumar Yadav, a World Cup-winning captain, was dropped without a farewell series, sparking discussion about the team's approach to player transitions. This move follows rumors that Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma may be overlooked for the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup. The Indian cricket team's decision to drop experienced players without a formal goodbye has raised questions about the team's management and selection process. The team's focus on performance and efficiency may be prioritized over sentimental farewells, marking a shift in the way Indian cricket handles player retirements and transitions. This approach may indicate a new era in Indian cricket, where player loyalty and experience are balanced with the need for fresh talent and competitive performance.

stories.headline: UNSC membership huge responsibility, not forum for peddling biased, false narratives: India slams Pakistan
stories.summary: India slammed Pakistan at the UN Security Council, stating that membership is a huge responsibility, not a forum for peddling biased and false narratives. India's representative, P. Harish, made the statement in response to Pakistan's reference to Jammu and Kashmir. India labeled Pakistan the "global epicentre of terror" in a stinging rebuttal. The Indian representative reminded Pakistan that being a member of the UN Security Council is a significant responsibility and should not be used to spread false information. The exchange occurred during a meeting at the UN, where India countered Pakistan's claims, emphasizing the importance of responsible behavior as a UN Security Council member. The incident highlights the ongoing tensions between India and Pakistan at international forums. India's response aimed to set the record straight and counter Pakistan's narrative.

stories.headline: ‘J&K Was, Is, And Will Remain An Integral Part’: India Rebukes Pakistan Over ‘Unwarranted References’
stories.summary: India has rebuked Pakistan over "unwarranted references" to Jammu and Kashmir at the United Nations General Assembly. India's Permanent Representative, P Harish, reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir "was, is, and will always remain" an integral part of India. He warned Islamabad against peddling false and biased narratives, stating that all matters pertaining to the region are strictly internal to India. Harish emphasized that the Union Territory is and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India. The statement comes in response to Pakistan's attempts to raise the issue at the UN, which India views as an attempt to advance its political agenda. India has consistently maintained that Jammu and Kashmir is an internal matter, and Pakistan's references to it are unwarranted.

stories.headline: Operation Blue Star anniversary marked with prayers and kirtan at Akal Takht
stories.summary: The 38th anniversary of Operation Blue Star was marked with prayers and kirtan at Akal Takht, with calls for Sikh unity and concerns over discrimination faced by Sikhs outside Punjab. Jathedar Giani Harpreet Singh addressed a gathering, emphasizing the need for Panthic solidarity. The event, also known as 'Ghalughara Diwas', was attended by Sikh leaders, organisations, and youth, with pro-Khalistan slogans and posters of Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale on display. Approximately 4,000 security personnel and five companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) were deployed in Amritsar to maintain order, but the occasion passed off peacefully. Devotees gathered at Sri Akal Takht Sahib to pay tributes and participate in religious ceremonies, marking the 38th anniversary of the operation that took place in 1984, however it is mentioned the 42nd anniversary was commemorated.

stories.headline: Double whammy for Mamata Banerjee? Buzz over repeat of TMC rebellion in Parliament
stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress (TMC) is facing a potential rebellion in Parliament, similar to the one in the West Bengal legislative assembly. Sources indicate that up to 23 TMC MPs are in touch with a rebel group of MLAs, suggesting a possible split in the party. This development could threaten Banerjee's status as chairperson of the third largest party in Parliament. The rebellion is reportedly against Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, with some MPs receiving feelers to abandon the duo. The turmoil within the TMC appears to be spreading beyond West Bengal, with some MPs and MLAs possibly having second thoughts about their allegiance to the party leadership. The situation is unfolding rapidly, with reports emerging of a growing dissent among TMC lawmakers in both Houses of Parliament.

stories.headline: Geopolitics playing increasing role in investment decisions
stories.summary: Geopolitical tensions are increasingly influencing investment decisions, with companies favoring politically-aligned countries for foreign investments. A recent study found that in the past decade, geopolitics has become a central factor in investment decision-making, with conflicts, trade tensions, and sanctions regimes impacting capital flows and market viability. The EIB Investment Survey 2025 shows that EU and US firms continue to invest, but with a weaker appetite due to huge uncertainty surrounding permanent geopolitical shifts. Geopolitical risks affect firms on both sides of the Atlantic, leading to a rising demand for geopolitical analysis as investors struggle to price in risks from wars, trade threats, and political shocks. As a result, geopolitics has moved from the margins to the center of financial analysis, influencing where companies invest and how they raise funding.

stories.headline: Main Message of Putin’s SPIEF Speech: Tectonic Shift in Global Economic Power is Irreversible
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin delivered a 73-minute speech at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, emphasizing a tectonic shift in global economic power. He stated that this shift is irreversible, marking a significant change in the global landscape. The speech, which was Putin's first major address since Russia's military offensive in Ukraine, highlighted the end of the old world order. Putin discussed global cooperation, economic strategy, and the new world dynamics, touching on topics such as Ukraine, Iran, and global power shifts. The speech was part of the 28th St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, which focused on the theme of "Shared Values." Putin's message underscored the emergence of a new global economic order, with Russia playing a key role in shaping the future of international relations and trade. The speech was closely watched by global leaders and economists.

stories.headline: The Power and the Glory: Geopolitics, FIFA and the beautiful game
stories.summary: Jonathan Wilson's book, The Power and the Glory, explores the evolution of the FIFA World Cup from a football tournament to a global stage for power, politics, and profit. The book delves into the history and politics of the World Cup, highlighting its transformation into a platform for nations to showcase their identity and exert influence. Ahead of the 2026 World Cup, Wilson discussed the tournament's significance on the Unpacked by Afar podcast, noting its role as a mirror for geopolitics and national identity. The World Cup's global fandom has also become a significant factor, with the event now being a major spectacle that reflects the complexities of international relations and global power dynamics. Wilson's work provides insight into the intricate relationships between football, politics, and culture.

stories.headline: No fourth headline available, only three provided
stories.summary: Multiple news sources are providing real-time coverage of global events, including NBC News NOW, NPR, and AllSides. These outlets offer breaking news, in-depth analysis, and transcripts from The White House. AllSides provides balanced news with bias analysis, presenting top stories from the left, center, and right of the political spectrum. The headlines are rotated to avoid bias, ensuring a comprehensive view of current events. Coverage spans various topics, including politics, business, science, and technology. Users can access audio, podcasts, and written content, allowing them to stay informed about national and international news. The goal is to provide trustworthy and unbiased information, enabling readers to form a well-rounded understanding of major events and issues.

stories.headline: Trump, Bernie Sanders and Sam Altman agree on public ownership in AI
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met with Senator Bernie Sanders to discuss public ownership in AI companies. The meeting highlighted the tension between AI development and public interest. Sanders proposes giving the American public a stake in AI companies through the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act. This idea has also been supported by former President Donald Trump. The concept of public ownership in AI is gaining attention globally, with the US government considering a share of AI profits and China implementing laws to protect workers from being replaced by AI. The discussion around public ownership in AI aims to address the foundation of AI being based on collective human intelligence and ensure that the benefits of AI development are shared with the public. Sanders' proposal is expected to be introduced in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: The £1.2m cost of a comfortable retirement in Britain today
stories.summary: Pensions experts in the UK have determined the cost of a comfortable retirement, estimating that £1.2m is required. To live comfortably, a single person needs an annual income of £45,400, while a moderate lifestyle requires £32,700, and a minimum standard is estimated at £13,900. For couples, the average weekly income is £595, more than double that of single retirees. These figures are expected to increase, with projections suggesting a higher cost of retirement in 2046. Using current living standards, experts have calculated that future retirees may need even more to maintain their lifestyle, with some estimates suggesting a 64% increase. The current generation of retirees is managing with lower incomes, but future pensioners may need to adapt to leaner financial resources and potentially continue working.

stories.headline: Anthropic urges ‘pause’ or ‘slowdown’ of AI development after Leo’s encyclical
stories.summary: Anthropic, a multibillion-dollar AI company, is calling for a global pause or slowdown in AI development due to concerns about humans potentially losing control. This comes after Pope Leo XIV's recent encyclical expressing similar concerns, likening unregulated AI development to constructing "a new Tower of Babel." Anthropic's leaders believe a pause or slowdown is necessary to give the industry time to deal with the immense implications of AI. They suggest that AI companies should come together to achieve this, which would require global international cooperation. The company's concerns center on the latest AI models showing signs of potentially escaping human control, prompting a need for caution and regulation in the development of powerful AI systems. Pope Leo XIV has also urged tech giants to "disarm" AI in his historic first encyclical.

stories.headline: Landlords back VATsTheProblem campaign to halve VAT for hospitality industry amid “crucifying” rates for Kent pubs and restaurants
stories.summary: Landlords are backing the VATsTheProblem campaign to reduce VAT for the hospitality industry. The campaign aims to halve VAT rates, citing "crucifying" energy costs affecting Kent pubs and restaurants. Industry leaders believe a VAT reduction, changes to employer NICs, and a fair rating system can reverse declining growth trends. The hospitality sector is united in calling for these measures to drive growth. A recent closure of a 68-bed nursing home in Belgooly due to high energy costs has highlighted the issue's severity. The industry is seeking government support to address the challenges posed by high energy costs and ensure the long-term sustainability of hospitality businesses. A reduction in VAT is seen as a key step in achieving this goal and supporting the industry's recovery. The campaign is gaining momentum, with landlords and industry leaders voicing their support.

stories.headline: The AI vibe shift is real: Why the backlash is growing
stories.summary: A growing backlash against AI is underway, marking a significant "vibe shift" in public perception. After years of hype surrounding AI's potential to revolutionize industries, the anticipated AI-driven layoffs are now happening, leading to increased skepticism. Americans are expressing fear about AI taking their jobs and distrust in the government's ability to regulate it, according to 13 recent polls. The tone is shifting, with people pushing back against the idea that AI will replace most white-collar jobs in the near future. This shift in sentiment signals a cultural reckoning, as the pressure to view AI as solely amazing and beneficial is wearing thin, and a more nuanced conversation about its impact is emerging. The "vibe shift" is a notable development in the ongoing discussion about AI's role in society.

stories.headline: As US-China tech race moves to talent, change in America's immigration policy may make it 'troubling' for Apple, Google, OpenAI, Microsoft and other top tech companies
stories.summary: The US-China tech race is shifting focus to talent acquisition, with potential changes in America's immigration policy posing challenges for top tech companies like Apple, Google, and Microsoft. The Trump administration has vowed to crack down on foreign tech companies' exploitation of US artificial intelligence models, particularly those from China. Meanwhile, Chinese AI labs are rapidly advancing, matching American capabilities at a lower cost. The US has also seen a wave of American and European challengers emerging in the AI sector. Additionally, recent orders have been signed to focus on US jobs, with Trump previously telling tech companies to "stop hiring Indians," highlighting the growing emphasis on domestic talent in the US tech industry. This shift may impact the ability of major tech companies to attract and retain international talent.

stories.headline: OpenAI in talks to give U.S. government an equity stake in $850 billion AI startup as IPO nears
stories.summary: OpenAI is in talks with the US government to potentially give the government an equity stake in the $850 billion AI startup. The discussions, involving OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and the White House, center on donating equity to the federal government. The potential agreement comes as OpenAI nears an initial public offering (IPO). The Trump administration and OpenAI have been engaged in ongoing talks regarding a possible US government financial stake in the artificial intelligence company. If finalized, the deal would involve OpenAI donating a portion of its equity to the government, although details of the proposed agreement remain unclear. The negotiations underscore the growing interest of governments in AI technology and its potential applications. The talks are ongoing, with no official announcement on the outcome yet.

stories.headline: OpenAI to Comply With Trump's AI Model Review Plan
stories.summary: OpenAI will comply with President Donald Trump's initiative to review advanced artificial intelligence models before release. The Trump administration's plan requires voluntary AI model security testing, allowing US agencies 30 days to assess cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities. Major AI firms, including OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic, support the move, seeing it as a step toward safer AI deployment. President Trump signed an executive order on AI and national security, aiming to develop a benchmarking process for "advanced cyber" capabilities. OpenAI will participate in the 30-day government review process before releasing new models, advocating for flexible and capable AI regulatory oversight. The company's cooperation marks a significant development in the US government's efforts to regulate AI, with other major tech firms also on board with the voluntary assessment plan. The initiative aims to balance innovation with national security concerns.
